# Flyology Runtime

> Flyology Runtime is an experimental GNAT runtime extension for ordinary Ada tasking. It combines interoperable native and lightweight execution lanes with task-aware I/O while preserving ordinary Ada task semantics and synchronous control flow.

Flyology uses the terms "lightweight task" and "native task." Lightweight scheduling is cooperative, not preemptive. The project does not claim production qualification, universal portability, or hard real-time behavior. Runtime preparation supports only the exact host and compiler release pairs documented by the project; do not infer support from the broader Alire dependency range.

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://flyology.org/): Project scope, programming model, included building blocks, and important constraints.
- [Guide](https://flyology.org/guide/): Toolchain requirements, runtime preparation, task designation, stack and memory policy, execution groups, task-aware I/O, resource budgets, observability, verification, and constraints.
- [Shared-memory segments](https://flyology.org/guide/shared-memory/): Anonymous, named POSIX, and file-backed storage; mapping and descriptor ownership; race-safe named extents; SCM_RIGHTS handoff; persistence; teardown; trust; blocking; and recovery limits.
- [Relocatable data structures](https://flyology.org/guide/data-structures/): Caller-owned backing regions, address-independent layouts, fixed arenas over selectable buddy, best-fit, and two-level segregated-fit allocation, arena-backed adaptive slab pools, bounded and arena-backed byte containers, synchronization models, application envelopes, attachment, relocation, poisoning, and recovery boundaries.
- [Architecture](https://flyology.org/architecture/): Tasking integration, native and lightweight lanes, schedulers, pollers, stackful contexts, memory ownership, and lifecycle boundaries.
- [Structured task supervision](https://flyology.org/guide/supervision/): Typed static trees, bounded dynamic families, readiness, generation-safe replacement, dependency and cohort recovery, incident budgets, stopping, and event rings.
- [Timers and clock changes](https://flyology.org/guide/timers/): Relative, monotonic, bounded multi-deadline, and wall-clock timer behavior, including complete due activation batches and backward clock changes.
- [File-to-socket transfers](https://flyology.org/guide/file-transfers/): Positional regular-file transfer loops, buffer ownership, deadlines, cancellation, native sendfile, Linux lightweight SEND_ZC, fallbacks, and reproducible measurements.
- [Benchmarking Ada](https://flyology.org/guide/benchmarking/): Adaptive batching, nanosecond-scale measurement semantics, balanced or sequential comparisons of two to sixteen implementations, externally controlled span recording, live terminal telemetry, collection budgets, and CSV or JSON output.
- [Cache-line-aware storage](https://flyology.org/guide/cachelines/): Standalone padded values, ownership-aware groups, host cache queries, and the Linux/macOS support boundary.
- [API reference](https://flyology.org/api/): Generated reference for Flyology's public Ada packages.
- [flyology_bench API reference](https://flyology.org/api/flyology_bench/): Generated reference for the benchmark configuration, measurement, comparison, baseline, metadata, host-control, and reporting APIs.
- [flyology_cachelines API reference](https://flyology.org/api/flyology_cachelines/): Generated reference for cache spacing, padded values, ownership-aware groups, grouped arrays, and host cache queries.

## Project sources

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/README.md): Detailed user-facing architecture, configuration, APIs, examples, constraints, and verification commands.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology): Ada sources, runtime integration, tests, proof model, scripts, showcases, and website sources.
- [Supported runtime patch matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/runtime/patches/README.md): Exact verified host, compiler, and GNAT runtime patch families.
- [Alire crate manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flyology-ada/flyology/main/alire.toml): Package metadata and dependency constraints; these constraints are broader than the verified runtime matrix.
- [Flyology Cachelines crate](https://github.com/flyology-ada/flyology/tree/main/flyology_cachelines): Standalone `flyology_cachelines` crate, tests, benchmarks, and public API sources.

## Optional

- [Development journal](https://flyology.org/journal/): Reserved for future runtime records, with links to the active HTTP and Postgres library journals.
- [Flyology HTTP](https://http.flyology.org/): A separate HTTP/1.1 client and application-server library built on Flyology task-aware I/O.
- [Flyology Postgres](https://postgres.flyology.org/): A separate ecosystem project exploring PostgreSQL access with Flyology.
